metadata.title: Claude, Wrap Up.
metadata.subtitle: The Wrap-Up Skill (Claude Managed Agents)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you tell Claude to wrap up your agent on Claude Managed Agents, does Claude shut the project down, or hand back a recap you can ask for again — and what does that recap actually check? Lands the carry-out that wrapping up isn't a shutdown, it's a re-runnable recap that only refreshes what's already there.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes wrapping up your agent means Claude closes the project down for good. It doesn't — it recaps where things stand, and you can run it again any time. So: a recap, not a shutdown?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is called wrap-up. The SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

Inside the SKILL.md is the pipeline. Claude runs it in order: refresh the overview page, recap every primitive you now own, show the run log and live status, suggest one or two tailored upgrades, then sweep hygiene — old sessions archived, the key kept only in dot-env, no literal dates left in deployment kickoffs.

Because wrap-up is idempotent, running it again doesn't start the build over or duplicate anything — it refreshes the same overview page and status tables. Same input, same output, every run. And it only recaps and suggests: it doesn't build the upgrades it names, and it only checks what the SKILL.md tells it to check.
Wrapping up your agent isn't a shutdown — it's a recap you can re-run any time, and running it again only refreshes what's already there.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to close out — or check in on — a Claude Managed Agent build. Refresh the overview page, recap every primitive I now own, show the run log and live status, suggest one or two tailored next upgrades, and sweep hygiene: archive old sessions, keep the key only in dot-env, and use no literal dates in deployment kickoffs. Read the wrap-up skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters — explaining first surfaces the hygiene sweep before Claude runs it.
